title: Smith bases for arbitrary-rank submodules over a PID
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative principal ideal domain, meaning a commutative ring with $1\ne0$, no zero divisors and every ideal principal. Let $M$ be an $R$-module with a basis indexed by a finite set [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $N\subseteq O\subseteq M$ be $R$-submodules (additive subgroups closed under scalar multiplication). There exist integers $0\leq n\leq o$, bases $(v_i)_{0\leq i<n}$ of $N$ and $(e_j)_{0\leq j<o}$ of $O$, and scalars $a_i\in R$ such that, as elements of $M$, $$v_i=a_i e_i\qquad(0\leq i<n).$$ No equality of the ranks of $N$ and $O$ is assumed; either submodule may be zero.

from.place: det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Power lifting and finite generation for PGL invariants. Supporting argument: Haboush symmetric-power lifting for a trivial quotient representation. Supporting representation-theoretic input: Central covering of a reductive group by a torus and a simply connected semisimple group. Milne central-cover construction: Multiplication by a central torus with semisimple quotient and the derived group. Supporting input: Semisimple algebraic groups are perfect. Root-subgroup structure and the torus conjugation formula used to realize the rank-one commutator calculation in Milne Corollary 21.50. Supporting lemma: Integration and comparison of a positive ray of torus weights. Milne p.348: the subtorus attached to the rational line of a character; choose primitive character coordinates using Smith normal form.
